entries.note: D13 drives the LED. Arduino sends 0/1 over Serial; the p5 circle follows that received value. Run and compare the two.
entries.title: 1 · HelloLED: one output

entries.note: Find pinMode(13, OUTPUT), digitalWrite and Serial.println in Arduino. In p5, acceptLine converts the complete serial line to a number. Change the delays later to test faster/slower blinking.
entries.title: Read the code

entries.note: The button is digital input, the LED is digital output, the pot is analog input and RGB brightness uses PWM output. INPUT_PULLUP means a pressed button reads LOW.
entries.title: 2 · Four signals: inputs and outputs

entries.note: The pressed button lights the separate LED. A low potentiometer value dims the PWM RGB output; watch the matching dashboard readings.
entries.title: Press and dim

entries.note: Release the button: digital LED off. Raise the pot: RGB gets brighter while its three PWM channels crossfade. Serial CSV is button,pot,LED,R,G,B.
entries.title: Release and brighten

entries.note: Arduino sends pot, distance and switch readings to the p5 spring field. p5 sends RGB commands back; Arduino scales them by the pot and reports the applied output and ACK.
entries.title: 3 · Field / feedback: close the loop

entries.note: High pot: more spring tension and brighter applied RGB. Near sonar: tighter preferred spacing. Toggle the switch to reverse circulation; motion continues in both states.
entries.title: Shape the field

entries.note: The telemetry reports applied R/G/B and ACK. D13 indicates recent accepted color commands. Requested color and applied output differ because the pot scales brightness. Try the Hue slider and Plots in the p5 canvas yourself.
entries.title: Read the return path

entries.note: Choose one mapping to change: blink delay, pot-to-PWM brightness, or distance-to-spring spacing. Predict the effect, edit the code, then run and compare. This replay controls simulation only; no hardware or permissions are requested.
entries.title: Your turn
